narration: You are born in a dark underwater cave off the coast of the Pacific Northwest.
scene: A tiny octopus egg hanging in a dark underwater cave, strands of eggs on the ceiling
label: PACIFIC NORTHWEST

narration: You are one of tens of thousands of eggs hanging from the ceiling like a curtain of rice.
scene: Long white strands of tiny eggs hanging from a cave ceiling like a curtain
label: A CURTAIN OF RICE

narration: Your mother laid somewhere between fifty and a hundred thousand of you.
scene: Huge mother octopus beside a massive cluster of tiny egg dots
label: 100,000 EGGS

narration: You are not special. You are a number.
scene: One tiny egg highlighted among thousands, an arrow pointing at it
label: NOT SPECIAL

narration: You hatch at the size of a grain of rice.
scene: Tiny rice-grain-sized octopus next to an actual grain of rice for comparison
label: GRAIN OF RICE

narration: You have no mother waiting. Actually, you have the opposite.
scene: Empty cave with a tiny hatchling alone, no mother in sight
label: NO ONE'S COMING

narration: Your mother is still there, wrapped around the eggs, and she is starving to death on purpose.
scene: Mother octopus wrapped around her eggs, looking thin and pale
label: STARVING ON PURPOSE

narration: She has not eaten in six months.
scene: Calendar with six months crossed out beside a thin mother octopus
label: 6 MONTHS, NO FOOD

narration: By the time the last of your siblings breaks free, she will be dead.
scene: Fading mother octopus while tiny hatchlings swim away from the eggs
label: SHE WON'T MAKE IT

narration: You drift upward, away from the den, into open water. Congratulations, you're alive. For now.
scene: Tiny hatchling drifting up out of a cave into open blue water
label: FOR NOW

narration: For the first few months, you are not an octopus. You are plankton.
scene: Tiny larval octopus drifting among specks of plankton
label: PLANKTON

narration: You float near the surface, at the mercy of the current.
scene: Tiny larva bobbing in ocean waves at the surface
label: AT THE MERCY

narration: A drifting fleck in the most crowded soup on Earth.
scene: Dense ocean full of tiny drifting creatures, one little octopus among them
label: THE SOUP

narration: Everything eats you. Fish. Jellyfish. Other octopus larvae.
scene: Big fish, jellyfish and other larvae all eyeing a tiny octopus
label: EVERYONE EATS YOU

narration: Birds dive from above. Even things with no mouth want you dead.
scene: A bird diving from the sky toward the water, tiny octopus below
label: FROM ABOVE

narration: The ocean is a buffet, and you are the appetizer.
scene: A long buffet table made of fish, tiny octopus as the appetizer plate
label: THE APPETIZER

narration: This is the slaughterhouse stage, and the math is not in your favor.
scene: Tiny octopus with a big grim calculator and crossed-out numbers
label: BAD MATH

narration: Out of every hundred thousand of you that hatch, one or two make it.
scene: Huge number 100,000 with one tiny octopus surviving beside it
label: 1 OR 2 SURVIVE

narration: Read that again. Your survival odds are worse than a lottery ticket.
scene: A losing lottery ticket next to a tiny octopus
label: WORSE THAN LOTTERY

narration: You do the only thing you can do. You drift.
scene: Tiny octopus drifting passively in the current, doing nothing
label: DRIFT

narration: You eat what's smaller than you and avoid being eaten by what's bigger.
scene: Tiny octopus eating a spec while a bigger creature looms behind
label: EAT SMALLER

narration: You grow. Every day you get a little less helpless.
scene: Octopus larva growing slightly bigger day by day, shown in three sizes
label: GROWING

narration: Weeks pass. Maybe months.
scene: A calendar flipping through weeks while the larva grows
label: WEEKS LATER

narration: Then, if you're still alive, you sink.
scene: Young octopus sinking down toward the dark seafloor
label: SINK

narration: You settle on the seafloor and start acting like an octopus.
scene: Young octopus landing on a rocky seafloor
label: SEAFLOOR

narration: Your first job is the same as every octopus's first job: find a den before something finds you.
scene: Young octopus searching the rocks for a hiding spot
label: FIND A DEN

narration: A den is just a hole. A crack in the rocks. An empty shell. A discarded bottle, if you're lucky.
scene: A rock crack, an empty shell and a bottle as possible homes
label: HOME OPTIONS

narration: You squeeze into it and learn the one trick that will keep you alive forever.
scene: Octopus squeezing into a narrow crack in the rock
label: SQUEEZE

narration: You have no bones. The only hard part of your entire body is your beak.
scene: Diagram of a soft octopus with a single hard beak highlighted
label: ONE HARD PART

narration: If your beak fits through a gap, the rest of you does too. You are a liquid that can think.
scene: Octopus pouring through a tiny gap like liquid
label: LIQUID BRAIN

narration: You spend your first year hiding.
scene: Young octopus tucked inside a den, one eye peeking out
label: HIDING

narration: You change color to match the rocks.
scene: Octopus blending into a rock, half visible
label: BLEND IN

narration: Your skin is covered in thousands of tiny pigment cells called chromatophores.
scene: Close-up of octopus skin with tiny colored dots labeled
label: CHROMATOPHORES

narration: You can turn them on and off faster than you can blink.
scene: Two octopuses, one flashing colors, one human eye blinking
label: FASTER THAN A BLINK

narration: You are the best camouflage artist on the planet, and you use it to be invisible.
scene: Octopus wearing a painter's beret, half invisible against the rocks
label: CAMO ARTIST

narration: You eat crabs, shrimp, and small fish.
scene: Young octopus eyeing a crab, shrimp and small fish on a plate
label: MENU

narration: You catch them by pouncing, by reaching, by being faster than they expect.
scene: Octopus pouncing on a startled crab
label: POUNCE

narration: You have three hearts pumping blue blood through your body.
scene: Diagram of an octopus with three hearts and blue blood vessels
label: 3 HEARTS

narration: You have nine brains — one in your head and one in each arm.
scene: Octopus with nine glowing brain dots: one in head, one per arm
label: 9 BRAINS

narration: Two-thirds of your neurons live in your arms, which means your arms basically make their own decisions.
scene: Octopus arms each with a little thinking bubble of their own
label: ARMS THINK

narration: You are a genius. You are also a snack.
scene: Octopus wearing graduation cap, then a small snack wrapper
label: GENIUS SNACK

narration: A sea otter would eat you for breakfast. Literally.
scene: Sea otter floating on its back, holding a tiny octopus over its belly
label: OTTER BREAKFAST

narration: By year two, you are no longer the bottom of the food chain.
scene: Octopus stepping up a rung on a food-chain ladder
label: MOVING UP

narration: By now you're a proper octopus, about a foot or two across.
scene: Octopus stretched out with a ruler showing one to two feet
label: 1–2 FEET

narration: And you've learned to hunt.
scene: Octopus in a hunting stance, arms spread, ready
label: HUNTER

narration: You hunt at night.
scene: Moonlit ocean floor, octopus moving in the dark
label: NIGHT HUNT

narration: You use your suckers — hundreds of them, each one able to taste and smell.
scene: Close-up of octopus arm suckers with little tongues and noses
label: SUCKERS TASTE

narration: To find a crab buried in the sand, you drift over it like a shadow.
scene: Octopus drifting over the sand above a hidden crab
label: SHADOW

narration: You spread your arms like a net.
scene: Octopus arms spreading wide into a net shape over the sand
label: THE NET

narration: And then you pounce.
scene: Octopus slamming down onto a crab
label: POUNCE

narration: You can catch several things at once.
scene: Octopus holding three different creatures in three arms at once
label: MULTITASK

narration: Each arm can hold something different while you decide which one to eat first.
scene: Octopus arms each holding food while the head has a thinking bubble
label: WHICH FIRST

narration: You are not a predator with one weapon. You are eight predators sharing a body.
scene: Eight small octopuses fused into one body, arms like separate hunters
label: EIGHT HUNTERS

narration: When a seal or a moray eel shows up, you don't fight. You run.
scene: Seal and moray eel approaching while the octopus flees
label: RUN

narration: Or you disappear into a hole no bigger than your beak.
scene: Octopus vanishing into a tiny hole in the rock
label: DISAPPEAR

narration: If a predator grabs an arm, you drop it. Seriously.
scene: Octopus leaving one arm behind in a predator's mouth as it swims free
label: DROP THE ARM

narration: You detach your own arm and swim away. It grows back.
scene: Octopus arm regrowing from a stub, shown in stages
label: IT GROWS BACK

narration: You also have a final trick: ink.
scene: Octopus squeezing out a puff of black ink
label: INK

narration: A cloud of black smoke that confuses the enemy while you jet away backwards.
scene: Black ink cloud hiding the octopus as it jets away
label: SMOKESCREEN

narration: You have the best escape kit in the ocean, and you use all of it.
scene: Octopus showing off its escape tools: camouflage, ink, jet propulsion
label: ESCAPE KIT

narration: Life is good. You're smart, you're fast, and you're invisible.
scene: Smug octopus leaning back, relaxed and confident
label: LIFE IS GOOD

narration: But you're also alone.
scene: Octopus alone in an empty patch of ocean
label: ALONE

narration: You've been alone your whole life, and you will be alone for the rest of it.
scene: Octopus with a long lonely shadow behind it
label: ALWAYS ALONE

narration: By year three, you are huge.
scene: Big octopus towering over a small fish
label: HUGE

narration: A full-grown giant Pacific octopus can stretch thirty feet across and weigh hundreds of pounds.
scene: Octopus stretched out with a thirty-foot measuring tape beside it
label: 30 FEET

narration: You are the biggest octopus on Earth.
scene: Octopus on a winner's podium with a gold medal
label: BIGGEST ON EARTH

narration: And everything in your neighborhood knows it.
scene: Small fish and crabs bowing as the big octopus passes
label: THE NEIGHBORHOOD

narration: You keep a den, and you decorate it with the leftovers of your kills.
scene: Octopus arranging shells and bones around the entrance of its den
label: DECORATING

narration: Crab shells, clam shells, fish bones — piled outside the door like trophies.
scene: A neat pile of shells and bones in front of a den, labeled as trophies
label: TROPHIES

narration: Other octopuses understand what that pile means: stay out.
scene: Another octopus reading the shell pile and backing away
label: STAY OUT

narration: You're clever in ways that shouldn't be possible.
scene: Octopus with a lightbulb above its head
label: TOO CLEVER

narration: You can unscrew a jar from the inside.
scene: Octopus inside a glass jar unscrewing the lid
label: JAR TRICK

narration: You can solve mazes.
scene: Octopus at the end of a small maze, arms tracing the path
label: MAZES

narration: You can carry coconut shells around and use them as armor.
scene: Octopus hiding inside two coconut shell halves like a helmet
label: COCONUT ARMOR

narration: You can recognize the humans who feed you, and you hold grudges against the ones who don't.
scene: Octopus smiling at one diver and spraying another with water
label: HOLD GRUDGES

narration: But none of it matters.
scene: Octopus's trophies and tricks fading into the background
label: DOESN'T MATTER

narration: Because something in your body is already counting down.
scene: A tiny timer ticking inside the octopus's body
label: COUNTDOWN

narration: You don't know it yet. But the clock started the day you were born.
scene: An hourglass running since a tiny egg, now nearly empty
label: THE CLOCK

narration: Mating season arrives. You don't choose it. Your biology does.
scene: Octopus with a calendar marked 'mating season', shrugging
label: MATING SEASON

narration: The optic gland — a tiny organ between your eyes — flips a switch.
scene: Diagram of an octopus head with the optic gland glowing like a switch
label: OPTIC GLAND

narration: And your body starts planning its own funeral.
scene: Octopus body holding a little coffin and funeral plan
label: FUNERAL PLAN

narration: If you're a male, you find a female.
scene: Male octopus approaching a larger female octopus
label: IF YOU'RE MALE

narration: You hand her a packet of sperm with one of your arms.
scene: Male octopus passing a small packet to the female with one arm
label: THE HANDOFF

narration: And then you die. Within weeks. Your body just stops.
scene: Male octopus fading and sinking away after the handoff
label: THEN YOU DIE

narration: If you're a female, you survive a little longer, but only to do the hardest job in the ocean.
scene: Female octopus looking at the viewer, carrying a big task ahead
label: IF YOU'RE FEMALE

narration: You find a den and lay your eggs — tens of thousands of them.
scene: Female octopus laying long strands of eggs on a den ceiling
label: LAYING EGGS

narration: You hang them from the ceiling in long white strands.
scene: White egg strands hanging from the den ceiling like curtains
label: THE STRANDS

narration: Then you stop eating.
scene: Female octopus pushing away a plate of food
label: NO MORE FOOD

narration: For six months, you do nothing but guard them.
scene: Female octopus wrapped around her eggs, unmoving
label: 6 MONTHS

narration: You fan water over them with your arms so they get oxygen.
scene: Female octopus waving her arms over the eggs to fan water
label: FANNING

narration: You chase off anything that comes close.
scene: Female octopus swatting away a curious crab near the eggs
label: GUARD

narration: You watch them grow while your own body eats itself.
scene: Eggs growing bigger while the mother shrinks thinner beside them
label: SHRINKING

narration: Your arms shrink. Your skin goes pale.
scene: Thin pale octopus with shrunken arms holding onto the eggs
label: PALE

narration: You waste away, one day at a time.
scene: Octopus getting thinner across a row of days on a calendar
label: WASTING AWAY

narration: Some mothers even start eating their own arms.
scene: Octopus with a fork biting its own arm, looking tired
label: EATING HERSELF

narration: And then, one day, they hatch.
scene: Eggs cracking open with tiny hatchlings emerging
label: THEY HATCH

narration: Thousands of tiny grains of rice drift up out of the den and into the current.
scene: Thousands of tiny hatchlings rising out of the den like bubbles
label: GOODBYE

narration: You watch them go. You don't follow.
scene: Weak mother octopus watching her hatchlings swim away
label: WATCHING

narration: You've done what an octopus does.
scene: Tired mother octopus with a soft, peaceful expression
label: JOB DONE

narration: You were born. You survived. You hunted. You hid. You mated.
scene: A row of icons: an egg, a fish, a crab, a cave, two octopuses
label: THE CHECKLIST

narration: You made the next generation.
scene: The checklist icon getting a final tick mark
label: THE NEXT GENERATION

narration: Your eyes close for the last time.
scene: Octopus closing its eyes gently
label: GOODNIGHT

narration: And you sink to the floor of your den.
scene: Lifeless octopus settling onto the den floor
label: THE END

narration: A crab walks in a few days later.
scene: A crab walking over the den floor past the old octopus
label: A CRAB

narration: It doesn't know it's standing on a genius.
scene: Crab standing on a faded octopus, clueless
label: STANDING ON A GENIUS

narration: As far as endings go, it could be worse.
scene: Octopus giving a small shrug from the afterlife
label: COULD BE WORSE

narration: At least you got to be the biggest, smartest, weirdest thing in the ocean.
scene: Octopus with a crown, a lightbulb, and a party hat
label: BIGGEST, SMARTEST, WEIRDEST

narration: Thanks for watching.
scene: Octopus waving goodbye with all eight arms
label: THANKS

narration: If you enjoyed this, consider subscribing.
scene: Octopus pointing at a big subscribe button
label: SUBSCRIBE

narration: And remember: the next time you see an octopus at an aquarium, just sitting there —
scene: Octopus sitting still in an aquarium tank, looking at the glass
label: AT THE AQUARIUM

narration: It's not lazy.
scene: Octopus shaking its head 'no' while sitting
label: NOT LAZY

narration: It's just waiting out a three-year countdown it can't stop.
scene: Octopus beside a timer counting down from three years
label: 3-YEAR COUNTDOWN

narration: A countdown every octopus is born with.
scene: A row of baby octopuses each with a tiny timer
label: BORN WITH IT

narration: And if you liked this, there's another animal that has it even worse.
scene: Octopus pointing off-screen to a mystery creature
label: NEXT TIME
